title: Lemon Caper Cream Sauce
description: A thick, glossy lemon caper sauce built to cling to mahi-mahi, chicken, or pasta, with plenty extra for spooning.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: to taste, go light because capers are salty

steps.title: Prep
steps.text: Zest the lemon for {zest}, then juice it for {lemon}. Drain the jar of capers and measure {capers} and {brine}. Have {broth} and {cream} measured and ready.

steps.title: Reheat the mahi
steps.text: Put the chilled mahi-mahi in the Anova Precision Oven at 120°F with 100% steam, bagless, with the probe in the thickest fillet. Cook until it reads 120°F to 125°F. Start checking at 20 minutes. Begin the sauce about 10 minutes before the fish is ready. Do not go above the original cook temperature or the fish will dry out.

steps.title: Melt the butter
steps.text: Melt {butter} in a stainless skillet or small saucepan over medium heat. Avoid bare cast iron here, because the lemon and capers will strip the seasoning and can taste metallic.

steps.title: Cook the garlic
steps.text: Add {garlic} and stir for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Jarred garlic burns quickly, so do not let it brown.

steps.title: Make the roux
steps.text: Whisk in {flour} and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until it smells slightly nutty. This is what gives the sauce body so it clings.

steps.title: Add the liquids
steps.text: Slowly whisk in {broth} so there are no lumps, then whisk in {cream}. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Stir in {umami}. If the sauce is thinner than you want, simmer another 1 to 2 minutes before moving on.

steps.title: Finish off the heat
steps.text: Remove the pan from the heat. Stir in {lemon} and {capers}, then add {butterfin} and swirl until melted and glossy. Adding the lemon off the heat keeps the flavor bright and keeps the cream from breaking. Taste, then adjust with {salt} and {pepper}.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pull the mahi when the probe reads 120°F to 125°F. If you want a little more heat in the center, finish it in a hot pan for a minute per side. Spoon a generous amount of sauce over the fish and top with {parsley}.

notes: Extra sauce is built in. If it is too thin, whisk 1 tsp cornstarch into 1 tbsp cold water and stir it in at a simmer for 1 minute. Make-ahead: the sauce keeps 2 days in the fridge. It thickens when cold, so rewarm gently over low heat with a splash of chicken broth and whisk until smooth. Also works on chicken piccata-style cutlets or Impastable pasta.
